articles.title: The Winamp Skin Museum lets you relive the wonderful chaos of late-’90s computing
articles.summary: Remember Winamp? Remember Winamp skins? If you grew up using a computer in the late ‘90s or early ‘00s, then you probably do. If so, the Winamp Skin Museum is for you — a nostalgic collection of some 65,000 skins, all fully interactive and usable.
articles.body: Every now and again, individuals of a certain generation (my generation) have a tendency to fall into a catatonic state whenever we remember Winamp skins. There’s just something about them that instantly transports one back to the late ‘90s / early ‘00s, when user interfaces were truly customizable, and your music collection was an endless and engrossing battle against garbled filenames like LINKIN_PORK-IN%THE%END(HQ).mp3. If any of that is triggering a nostalgic response, then you’ll probably enjoy the Winamp Skin Museum. It’s an endlessly scrolling collection of 65,000 Winamp skins, searchable and fully interactive. There’s a default playlist (which includes the “Llama Whippin’ Intro”), and you can even load audio files into it from your computer, if you happen to have any lying around. [Media: The skins were previously collected on the Internet Archive but assembled into this new accessible format by Facebook engineer Jordan Eldredge. On Twitter, Eldredge notes he’s still taking collections for the project if you have any skins you want to donate, and he describes the collection as capturing “an iconic moment in internet art history.” He’s not wrong. The taste on display in the Winamp Skin Museum is, in a word, stunning. It has all of the artistic value of a national art gallery, but it focuses in on late-’90s / early-’00s aesthetics with enough raw energy to bring back nü metal. On display, you can see anime skins, gaming skins, communist skins, sci-fi skins, skins dedicated to particular artists, and a cornucopia of indescribable vibes in between. The only disappointment is that the format of the museum doesn’t lend itself to supporting the stranger skins that transformed the size and shape of Winamp’s various elements. But perhaps that would have been too much for today’s modern, sleek UIs to handle. [Image: You can even load up visualizations. This is the weird thing about Winamp skins, though: they don’t just capture a visual aesthetic, but a mode of interaction with technology. Personally, they remind me of an era when it felt like I had more control over my computer. I could customize Winamp skins, sure, but also my whole desktop, down to my extremely carefully collated music collection. There was also something about having to sort through files and dig up album art that encouraged a sort of engagement with music that feels, to me, very different to today’s streaming model. Spotify, compared to Winamp, seems passive. You’ll get your Discover playlist, and you’ll like it. (And I do.) You could argue that we’ve traded into this chaotic customization for convenience. But was it worth it? Probably. Perhaps all I’m really missing is a period of my life when I had time and energy to mess about with that sort of thing. Arguably, computers are just as customizable, if you care to put in the effort. But you see what I mean, now? Winamp skins, dude. They really take you back.

articles.title: Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man gets community justice right
articles.summary: The most interesting thing about Disney Plus’ Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man is its focus on making Peter Parker a hero of the people.
articles.body: Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man star Hudson Thames left many eyebrows raised last week after his comments about fearing the Disney Plus series would be “annoying and woke.” During a subsequent Reddit AMA, series creator Jeff Trammell was quick to start doing damage control, and he insisted that Thames had misspoken. But even in its most charitable interpretation, Thames’ statement was pretty odd considering how being annoying and constantly vigilant about injustice are kind of Spider-Man’s whole schtick. We may never know exactly what Thames meant or whether his feelings could have been expressed more thoughtfully. But what’s funny about the entire situation is how Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man is, in fact, one of those “woke” shows you’re always hearing culturally conservative types harp on about. It celebrates multiculturalism by treating diversity as a simple fact of the world Peter Parker exists in. And the series’s “wokeness” is honestly one of the best things about it. There’s a lot of the Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man series that rings familiar if you’ve spent time reading Marvel’s comics or watched any of the studio’s multiple TV shows or films revolving around the webhead. It’s another story about Peter Parker (Thames), a dorky kid from Queens trying to balance a double life as both a high school student and a superhero. Some of the series’s worldbuilding details are a little different than what you might be used to; Aunt May (Kari Wahlgren) loses her husband before Peter is bitten by a strange spider, for example. But the show hits many of the classic Spider-Man beats, like Peter’s trademark bad luck and his aptitude for building gadgets like his webshooters. [Media: The show’s biggest changes come by way of the friends and rivals Peter makes as he bounces back and forth between classes at school and an internship at Norman Osborn’s (Colman Domingo) Oscorp. More traditional Spider-Man characters like Harry Osborn (Zeno Robinson) and Lonnie Lincoln (Eugene Byrd) are also in the mix. But this Peter is best buds with longtime Runaways fixture Nico Minoru (Grace Song), and both have crushes on Pearl Pangan (Cathy Ang) — a newer character who first appeared in Marvel’s War of the Realms comics event back in 2019. Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man is not the first instance of Marvel diversifying the cast of supporting characters around Peter Parker in order to make Spider-Man stories more inclusive and reflective of what life can be like in New York City. Those changes were part of what made 2008’s The Spectacular Spider-Man animated series and Marvel / Sony’s recent live-action Spider-Man films feel so modern compared to Stan Lee and Steve Ditko’s early Spider-Man comics from the ’60s in which the vast majority of characters were white. Your Friendly Neighborhood’s diversity isn’t the only thing it has going for it. The show’s action, though stutter-y at times, is fun and works well with its cel-shaded, comic book-inspired aesthetic that often presents shots as if they were panels from a physical book. But the series’s slight adjustments to Peter Parker’s world are what gives its story a level of depth and thoughtfulness — which could be considered “woke” — that is surprising to see from Marvel. It bears repeating that, even though the term “woke” has become a racist / sexist / homophobic catchall dogwhistle often used by bigots as a pejorative, the concept of staying woke originated within Black communities and refers to the importance of being able to recognize the societal dangers Black people face. Featuring characters who are Black, or merely non-white, does not automatically mean that a film or TV show has anything to say about things like policing, crime, and structural inequality. But Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man certainly does as it starts showing you what makes this Peter Parker more of a street-level vigilante than any of his big-screen counterparts. [Image: Even though certain characters’ names give you an idea of the more fantastical nonsense Peter’s going to end up dealing with as the season continues, one of the first bits of heroism we see from him in the premiere is a quick moment where he brings a thief back to a pizza joint she’s just robbed. The thief, a white woman, tells Peter that she’s become desperate after losing her job. Peter has no way to know if that story is true, but as part of a family dealing with their own money problems, he can understand how that kind of loss pushes people to the edge. That moment contrasts sharply with another scene where Lonnie, who is Black, is racially profiled in quick succession by both the police on the street and a random white woman on the train as he makes his way home. Through that juxtaposition of moments, Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man is actually saying a lot about how different styles of policing communities can lead to drastically different outcomes for their populations. The show does not need to depict the police attacking Lonnie to illustrate how racial profiling is a kind of violence in and of itself that causes real harm to the people who experience it. We also don’t need to know every detail of the pizza thief’s life to grasp the difficulty of her circumstances and see how Spider-Man was able to peacefully resolve a criminal situation by leading with empathy rather than suspicion. Before the concept of wokeness was co-opted and weaponized by the right, it was very easy to understand as being aware of and attentive to social inequalities that shape our world. Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man might not explicitly spell them out, but those ideas are baked into its take on Peter Parker. A lot of this — the focus on community, the desire to help rather than penalize — has always been part of the traditional Spider-Man brand. And Disney’s new show is doing an excellent job of making sure you don’t forget that.

articles.title: Aluno em SP agride funcionários e quebra academia na Oscar Freire | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo professor, homem foi ao local para cobrar um adiantamento que fez ao personal trainer; ele teria arremessado notebook contra gerente e retornado nesta manhã para depredar o estabelecimento.
articles.summary: Segundo professor, homem foi ao local para cobrar um adiantamento que fez ao personal trainer; ele teria arremessado notebook contra gerente e retornado nesta manhã para depredar o estabelecimento.
articles.body:
Um aluno de uma academia localizada na Rua Oscar Freire, 1411, em Pinheiros, área nobre de São Paulo , agrediu funcionários na última quarta-feira (7) e, nesta quinta-feira (8), retornou ao local e quebrou espelhos da unidade. Câmeras de segurança registraram o ataque (veja acima).

Pelas imagens, de ângulos diferentes, é possível ver que ele parte para cima do gerente, e depois é apartado por um professor. Ele também pega os pesos da academia e joga contra os espelhos. Alguns alunos saem correndo. Há ainda imagens dele arremeçando um notebook contra uma funcionária.

Segundo o gerente da academia, Rubens Abrego Lourenço da Silva, de 47 anos, o homem foi ao local inicialmente para cobrar um valor de R$ 1.300 que teria emprestado a um personal trainer que atende na unidade. O nome do agressor ainda não foi divulgado.

"O problema com esse aluno começou na segunda-feira. Ele contrata um personal e é aluno da academia, pagante da academia, e como aluno ele contrata um personal por fora, para ter a aula assistida. Aí ele diz que o personal solicitou R$ 1.300 emprestado para ele", afirmou o gerente em entrevista ao g1.

Aluno invade academia na Oscar Freire e quebra espelhos — Foto: Reprodução

De acordo com o relato, o personal teria pedido o adiantamento do valor, mas está afastado por problemas de saúde e não está indo ao local dar as aulas. O aluno, então, teria procurado a academia para cobrar o dinheiro.

O gerente disse que consultou a diretoria e recebeu a orientação de que a academia não poderia se responsabilizar pelo valor, já que o acordo teria sido feito diretamente entre o aluno e o personal trainer.

Segundo o gerente, o aluno não aceitou a explicação por telefone e foi até a academia cerca de 15 minutos depois da ligação. No local, ele teria ameaçado e agredido verbalmente funcionários.

"Deu 15 minutos ele foi na academia, começou a fazer um espetáculo lá na frente da recepção, chamar a gente de 'bandido', me chamou de 'ladrão', falou que a gente não paga para funcionar, começou a falar um monte de absurdo", declarou.

Ainda segundo o gerente, o homem passou a bater no balcão da recepção. A gerente começou a filmar a situação e, conforme o relato, ele teria tentado agredi-la algumas vezes.

"Ele viu que a gente não estava dando bola, começou a bater no balcão, a nossa gerente começou a filmar, ele ficou nervoso, tentou agredí-la duas, três vezes, na quarta vez ele pega o notebook que está na mesa, dá um tapa no notebook, acerta o peito dela", disse.

Gerente da academia onde aluno quebrou vidros e agrediu funcionários — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

O gerente afirmou que acionou a polícia durante a confusão. Ainda de acordo com o relato, o aluno teria entrado na área da recepção e dito que pegaria o dinheiro que estava na gaveta.

"Depois ele tenta invadir, falou que ia roubar o dinheiro de volta, que ia pegar o dinheiro da gaveta, e aí eu abordo ele lá, a gente começa uma luta corporal praticamente", contou.

O gerente disse que registrou um boletim de ocorrência sobre o episódio ocorrido na quarta-feira (7), mas que o homem não foi preso em flagrante.

Nesta quinta-feira (8), segundo o gerente, o aluno voltou à academia por volta das 7h e teria ameaçado os funcionários. Ele teria exigido que as imagens da confusão fossem apagadas.

"Hoje, ele voltou, ameaçando, 7h da manhã ele voltou, mandando apagar todas as imagens, que se continuar essas imagens ele ia acabar com todo mundo, ameaçando a gerente e a mim", afirmou.

Ainda segundo o gerente, cerca de 40 minutos depois, o homem retornou ao estabelecimento e começou a quebrar os espelhos da academia. Imagens mostram o momento em que alunos deixam o local durante o ataque.

O gerente e a gerente estão no 14º Distrito Policial, onde, segundo o relato, devem registrar boletim de ocorrência por agressão e danos ao patrimônio.

articles.title: Nana Patekar’s mortal remains brought to Pune for state funeral, Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis pays last respects, Eknath Shinde, 'Welcome' director Anees Bazmee and others arrive
articles.summary: Veteran actor Nana Patekar passed away on Thursday at the age of 75 after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa, was accorded a state funeral
articles.body: Veteran actor Nana Patekar passed away on Thursday at the age of 75 after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa, was accorded a state funeral in recognition of his contribution to theatre and cinema. His mortal remains have now been brought to Donje in Pune, where his last rites will be performed, and several celebrities and prominent personalities have begun arriving to pay their final respects.Nana Patekar suffered a cardiac arrest at his Goa residence and was given continuous CPR for around 45 minutes. He died at 5:20 am. His son, Malhar, confirmed the news to The Indian Express and said, “Yes, the information is true. I am in Pune right now and reaching Goa. I will come up with detailed statement. He died due to natural reasons."Maharashtra Cultural Affairs Minister Ashish Shelar announced that Nana would be accorded a state funeral, recognising his immense contribution to theatre and cinema. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis also paid his last respects to the actor at Pune Airport after his mortal remains arrived from Goa.The mortal remains were subsequently taken from the airport to Donje village, where the final rites are being held. As Nana’s mortal remains have reached the farmhouse, members of the film industry and political fraternity have started arriving to pay their last respects to the veteran actor.Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde was among the first prominent personalities to reach the venue for Nana Patekar’s funeral. More celebrities and well-wishers are expected to arrive in Donje as the actor’s final journey continues. Filmmaker Anees Bazmi, actor-director Pravin Tarde, Prasad Oak among others were also spotted at the funeral.Nana Patekar's last films will be 'Shakti Shalini' starring Aneet Padda and 'Eetha' starring Shraddha Kapoor.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Exclusive: Dimple Kapadia on Nana Patekar: He was generous & brutally honest, perhaps why he was often misunderstood
articles.summary: Dimple Kapadia and Nana Patekar worked together in four films, including Krantiveer (1994) and Prahaar: The Final Attack (1991), both of which became
articles.body: Dimple Kapadia and Nana Patekar worked together in four films, including Krantiveer (1994) and Prahaar: The Final Attack (1991), both of which became iconic for capturing the angst, frustration and helplessness of common man and the middle class. Prahaar was the only feature film Nana directed in his career, with Dimple, Madhuri Dixit and Gautam Joglekar among its cast.Shaken by the news of Nana’s untimely demise, Dimple says she is still struggling to process the loss. “It’s unbelievable. It’s not sinking in. I wanted to call him the other day, but I delayed it and now I can’t speak to him ever. I wish I had made that call. I won’t be able to get over this.”Looking back at their journey and friendship, she recalls Nana as an actor and co-star who was deeply invested in his colleagues. “He was a fine actor and a great co-star who was always giving. It was wonderful to work with him because he wasn’t selfish. He cared about how I would look in a scene too, and how my character came across. That’s rare.”On a personal note, she says, “Nana was brutally honest. He never minced his words. If he wanted to say something to you, he would say it to your face. That was perhaps why he was often misunderstood. But he always said things for your own good. The intent was your bhalai. He wasn’t rude, just unfiltered and well-intentioned. There was an angst all over his face, but he was extremely warm and caring as a person.”Dimple remembers several instances of his spontaneous interventions on set. “There was a courtroom scene in one of our films where I had to be teary-eyed, and he would yell at me from a distance, ‘Aiyee Dimpy, glycerine nahi use karneka.’” She laughs, recalling how Nana never hesitated to push his co-stars to give their best.She also remembers a scene in another film where Nana’s character was supposed to investigate hers. “I am shown putting my knitting needles aside when he enters. He saw the prop and started knitting himself. For a man to do that was powerful and spontaneous. It made the scene look organic and impactful.”Dimple is particularly grateful that she got to experience Nana not just as an actor but as a director. “I’m glad I was directed by Nana in Prahaar. Was he calm on set as a director? Not at all. He was totally mad,” she says with a smile. “But there was so much to learn from him as an artiste and as a person.”Reflecting on their much-loved pairing in Krantiveer, she adds, “We fed off each other’s energy in Krantiveer. This is such a great loss for Hindi cinema, Marathi cinema and theatre. I’m going to miss him and his simplicity.”Author: Renuka.Vyavahare@timesofindia.com Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Nana Patekar laid to rest with full state honours in Pune, Eknath Shinde offers floral tribute, Jackie Shroff and thousands of fans gather to bid tearful farewell to the legendary actor
articles.summary: Legendary actor Nana Patekar breathed his last on Thursday, October 8, at his residence in Goa at the age of 75.
articles.body: Legendary actor Nana Patekar breathed his last on Thursday, October 8, at his residence in Goa at the age of 75. The veteran actor suffered a cardiac arrest and doctors attempted to revive him with continuous CPR for around 45 minutes. He was declared dead at around 5:20 am.Nana’s son Malhar confirmed the news to The Indian Express and said, “Yes, the information is true. I am in Pune right now and reaching Goa. I will come up with detailed statement. He died due to natural reasons.”In recognition of his immense contribution to theatre and cinema, the Maharashtra government accorded Nana Patekar a state funeral. His mortal remains were brought to Pune, where his last rites were performed at his farmhouse in Donje with full state honours. Large numbers of fans gathered to pay their final respects to the actor, whose powerful performances over a career spanning several decades made him one of Indian cinema’s most respected performers.Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis paid his last respects to Nana at Pune Airport after his mortal remains arrived from Goa. Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde was also among the prominent personalities who reached the venue to bid farewell to the veteran actor.Nana’s death has also left the film fraternity mourning. Several Bollywood celebrities took to social media to remember the actor and share personal memories of him.Shah Rukh Khan, who worked with Nana in ‘Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman’ and ‘Shakti: The Power’, shared an emotional note recalling the veteran actor as his mentor, teacher, critic and friend. Remembering their first meeting, SRK wrote, “When I first met him, out of awe and awkwardness I fiddled with my hair. He slapped my hand away and said ‘hero ki tarah Baal mat bana...tu actor hai’!”He further remembered Nana’s candid nature and wrote, “He didn’t flatter you. He didn’t tell you what you wanted to hear. He told you what you needed to hear. That was Nana. Straightforward. Rough, honest and had the most beautiful smile.” SRK also recalled their carrom games and ended his tribute by calling Nana a “masterful actor and an unbeatable carrom champion.”Salman Khan also paid tribute to Nana on Instagram, sharing a picture of the late actor and writing, “Nanaaaaaaaaaaa. Rest in peace bhau…”Ajay Devgn, who shared screen space with Nana in films including ‘Apaharan’ and ‘Raajneeti’, posted an old picture with the actor and wrote, “Not many made us happy, sad and feel anger quite the way Nana did. His presence was powerful, his performances unforgettable, and his absence will now be deeply felt. Rest well, Nana…Om Shanti.”Several other members of the film fraternity, including Akshay Kumar, Paresh Rawal, Manisha Koirala, Manoj Bajpayee, Urmila Matondkar, Alia Bhatt, Kareena Kapoor Khan and Karan Johar, also remembered Nana Patekar on social media, mourning the loss of one of Indian cinema’s most distinctive and powerful actors.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Nana regaled city’s drama patrons too
articles.summary: Nana Patekar, who died Thursday, is remembered in Lucknow for theatre roles like ‘Purush’, which ran 16 years and revived audience interest.
articles.body: Lucknow: Long before Nana Patekar became known for his powerful dialogues — from “Yeh Musalman ka khoon, yeh Hindu ka khoon…” in Krantiveer in the 1990s to “Control Uday, control” in Welcome — he was a theatre actor.And Lucknow was among the cities that got to experience the actor up close. Nana, who died on Thursday, had a career, of which theatre was an important thread.For Lucknow’s theatre lovers, his legacy is also tied to the stage of Ravindralaya, where the city watched him perform ‘Purush’, the powerful Hindi play in which he played a corrupt politician and sexual predator.Talking to TOI, Lucknow-born theatre director and designer Salim Arif recalled his association with Nana and said his performance in ‘Purush’, which was staged in the city, revealed the extraordinary intensity of an actor who remained “simple and transparent” offstage. The play ran for more than 16 years and clocked around 1,860 shows, bringing together Patekar and actress Ayesha Jhulka. It was directed by celebrated theatre personality Vijaya Mehta.“The production was among the major plays by nationally known actors that came to the city and helped create a renewed appetite for theatre among Lucknow audiences,” said Arif, who worked with Patekar on Gulzar’s ‘Hu Tu Tu’, and said the actor brought value to every role he played.“Just like Rajkumar, Nana too had a distinct style,” he recalled. Patekar, he said, was far removed from the trappings of stardom and would often say that he needed only “200 bucks” to survive and was known for his generosity, even donating a substantial part of his fee to charity. On the sets of ‘Hu Tu Tu’, he would cook prawns and fish and feed the entire unit, Arif recalled. The actor’s simplicity extended to his personal life too, with Arif remembering how Patekar would stay in a modest one-room house during Ganpati celebrations, while his mother would insist that visitors eat before leaving.Veteran Lucknow actor Anil Rastogi, meanwhile, recalled watching Patekar perform on stage in two different productions in Lucknow. “He came to Lucknow twice for the love of theatre. One of his plays was ‘Ek Kunwara Shadi Shuda’, in which he played a servant. Interestingly, he also played a female character. The other play of his that I remember is ‘Purush’,” said Rastogi.Rastogi said he met Patekar during a dinner organised by Uttar Pradesh chief secretary Yogendra Narain. “I told him I was the co-sponsor of one of his plays. He was extremely happy and said, ‘Mera play dekhne wala mila koi.’ He had a great sense of humour,” Rastogi recalled.Theatre artist Shubham Singh Chauhan, who worked with Patekar in the 2022 movie titled ‘The Vaccine war’, said, “Working with Nana Patekar was a truly inspiring experience. His acting, dialogue delivery, pauses and breathing rhythm taught me the depth of a fine performance. Every moment around him was a lesson in the craft. articles.title: Demi Moore almost lost role in “St. Elmo’s Fire” to Madonna after showing up ‘drunk and high’ to fitting
articles.summary: The “Substance” actress previously opened up about having a 24/7 sober companion on the film.
articles.body:
Demi Moore was nearly replaced by Madonna in St. Elmo's Fire.

Director Joel Schumacher allegedly gave Moore an ultimatum: Get sober or get fired.

Moore chose to enter recovery and had a 24/7 sober companion on set.

Demi Moore had to shape up in order to keep her role in St. Elmo's Fire .

Otherwise, director Joel Schumacher would replace her. Troubles on set had begun a couple of weeks before shooting, as costume designer Susan Becker had alerted him to the fact that Moore showed up to a fitting "drunk and high."

"Joel and [producer] Lauren Shuler [Donner] met with Demi and what Joel told me, he told her is, 'Go kill yourself on someone else's movie,'" Carl Kurlander, the film's co-writer, said on the Thursday episode of Reality Life with Kate Casey , noting that Schumacher had his own experiences with addiction. "And Lauren Shuler Donner, God bless her, worked out a plan with Joel, saying, 'Look, if you can clean yourself up in 10 days you can be in this movie.'"

Entertainment Weekly reached out to representatives for Moore for comment.

In the meantime, the production needed to be ready with a backup plan. While he considered several candidates to play Jules, including some existing cast members like Jenny Wright, Schumacher apparently had his eyes set on Madonna.

"Joel had met Madonna. And he came back and he said, 'This girl is going to be the biggest star in the world. I could just feel it,'" Kurlander said. "And Joel was all ready to offer the part to Madonna."

But Moore was not going to give up her chance to be in the 1985 film. She got a sober companion and began attending AA meetings, proving to Schumacher that she was serious about her recovery.

"She clearly had more than just cleaned up," Kurlander said.

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

Moore has been open about her struggles with substance abuse in the past. In her 2019 memoir Inside Out , she wrote that by the mid '80s, "my appetite for cocaine had escalated into a dependency."

And in the Brats documentary in 2024, which documented the rise of the Brat Pack in the 1980s, Moore shared her perspective on having a sober companion during St. Elmo's Fire. She said that director Schumacher had "stuck his neck out for me" by allowing her to get better and stay in the movie.

"We were all just beginning," she said of herself and her costars. "I didn't have anything to really warrant him sticking by me. They paid to have a sober companion with me 24/7 during the whole shooting."

She was aware that Schumacher could recast her, so the 63-year-old was grateful to have a second chance. Moore would maintain her sobriety for over two decades before relapsing in 2012. After re-entering treatment, she has been sober ever since.

"They could have easily just found someone else," Moore said. "Going to treatment, they were like, 'We want you to check in.' I'm like, 'No, no, I'm starting a movie.' And they said, 'Yes, but what's more important to you: the movie or your life?' And I said, 'The movie! C'mon, what are you talking about?' For me, I didn't have any value for myself. I think I was so fearful of failing."

articles.title: Feige caught him.
articles.summary:
During Marvel Television’s presentation at this year’s New York Comic Con, the studio announced that it is developing a live-action series titled Zodiac that will debut in 2028. The new show’s still a ways out, but we can expect to see the second season of Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man on January 13th, 2027.

articles.title: Nana Patekar’s death case: Goa Police registers 'unnatural death' case; to record statements of family and conduct post-mortem to establish cause of death
articles.summary: The Goa Police have registered a medico-legal 'Unnatural Death' (UD) case in connection with the death of veteran actor Nana Patekar.
articles.body: The Goa Police have registered a medico-legal 'Unnatural Death' (UD) case in connection with the death of veteran actor Nana Patekar. As per the latest update on IANS, an inquiry is underway to establish the circumstances and exact cause of the actor's death.As per a post on the IANS official handle, a case has been registered under Section 194 of the BNSS, with PSI Nitin Naik conducting the inquiry. An entry in the case registered at Panjim, stated that the actor was “brought dead to the casualty from Ocean Park, Dona Paula. Accordingly visited the spot at Manipal Hospital Bambolim at concern ward and matter was discussed with Medical Officer.”As part of the investigation, police will conduct an inquest, arrange a post-mortem examination at Goa Medical College (GMC) and record statements from family members and other relevant persons to determine the cause of death.Police are currently examining the circumstances surrounding the actor’s death. If the investigation establishes that the death was due to natural causes, the case may be closed accordingly. However, if any evidence of foul play or other suspicious circumstances emerges, further legal action may follow.This update comes after Dr Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Oncology Department at Manipal Hospital, told the media early Thursday morning, "We tried here to our maximum, but he was brought dead and then we had to make a police case. The body has now been taken to the morgue in Goa Medical College for postmortem. It was a cardiac arrest, but we do not know the cause."The doctor also mentioned, "He was a known cardiac patient and was on medication, as far as we have been told."Patekar, died early Thursday morning after suffering a reported cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. Doctors at Manipal Hospital reportedly administered CPR for around 45 minutes in an attempt to revive him, however, he was declared dead at 5.20 am.The post-mortem examination was reportedly conducted on Thursday morning, after which the actor's mortal remains were released for his last rites. Patekar was cremated with full state honours at his farmhouse in Donje in Pune district late Thursday night. He was given a 3-gun salute.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Glen Powell wants no part of political fights that divide people
articles.summary: Glen Powell says political discourse is "the worst version of a conversation" and reveals how movies remain his preferred way to express himself.
articles.body: Glen Powell wants nothing to do with Hollywood's political firestorms. The "Top Gun: Maverick" star opened up about his decision to stay out of politics and why he believes the growing divide has made it nearly impossible to have a healthy conversation. "Over time, I realized that politics divide people," Powell told Esquire. "People trying to prove their point – for me, it’s the worst version of a conversation. I genuinely do not like the discourse. It’s not as healthy as it once was." DWAYNE 'THE ROCK' JOHNSON REJECTS HOLLYWOOD’S POLITICAL OBSESSION, BLASTS CELEBRITY ATTACK CULTURE For Powell, engaging in politics is "not presently possible." "I applaud people for jumping into those things and fighting for what they believe in," he added. "If I were a political person, I would be talking about it. For me, my calling is elsewhere." Powell's reluctance to wade into politics dates back to his upbringing. Despite his mother's work in the Reagan administration at the U.S. Treasury Department, the actor said politics and current events weren't regular topics of conversation around the family dinner table. He echoed the sentiment in a previous interview with The Guardian. "I’m not a political person," he said in October 2025. "I like things that bring people together." DOLLY PARTON REFUSED TO PICK POLITICAL SIDES FOR DECADES: ‘I’M NOT IN POLITICS, I’M AN ENTERTAINER’ With politics increasingly dividing audiences, even Hollywood's biggest stars are finding it harder to appeal to everyone. Powell weighed in on whether entertainment can still bring Americans together and if action movies are one of the last remaining escapes from the political divide. "That’s a good point. There’s a universal language of action, which is also why those movies translate so well internationally," he added. "'Running Man' is about something universal – what you would be willing to do for the people you love? But also how people can feel powerless in the face of a world that feels more and more unequal, more unfair." "So, you’re not going to see me talk politics. But movies – that’s how I express myself," he added. "Movies are a conversation; politics always felt to me like two people trying to prove a point." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Powell has become one of Hollywood's most recognizable leading men, thanks to standout performances in "Top Gun: Maverick," "Anyone But You" and "Twisters." Yet his stardom didn't light overnight. He once had a casting director tell him he'd be lucky to "play a dead body" on CSI as he struggled for a decade to get his foot in the door. "There was a point where I realized that acting is not a meritocracy," he said during an appearance on "CBS Mornings." And just because you exist on a longer timeline doesn't mean it's going to work out. Right? There's a lot of other bigger forces at play." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "The fact that all of those sort of detours along the way about learning how to sort of develop and raise money and write – all these things are now kind of leading me to a place where all of those weapons are at my disposal," he added. The Hollywood heartthrob kept his hot streak alive in 2026, starring alongside Margaret Qualley in the dark comedy thriller "How to Make a Killing" before lending his voice to Fox McCloud in "The Super Mario Galaxy Movie." The Texas-born star is gearing up for two major 2027 projects, including Judd Apatow's comedy "The Comeback King" and J.J. Abrams' sci-fi adventure "The Great Beyond." "Life is fast for both of us," he told Esquire. "And we have the same values. She loves her family. I love my family. And we both care about work a lot. We both like to show up for our partners. And yet we also understand the balance of it all." While both stars juggle demanding careers, Powell made it clear that having someone who understands the pressures of Hollywood is only part of the equation. "There’s something so lovely about someone rooting for you," he told the outlet. "Someone who wants you to win in all the ways that are good for you as a human. articles.summary: Ella Langley's bikini selfie and viral "not enough in the world" caption had fans cracking up during her Dandelion tour Instagram photo dump.

She then famously looked at him with a serious look on her face and said, "Not enough in the world," as she frowned and looked away. "HAHHAAH caption, poor guy shoulda known better," one fan wrote in the comments section, while another added, "The caption is everything 😂." Also included in the Instagram post were photos of Langley on stage, a video of a penguin giving her a hug, her and her friends goofing off in what seems like a trailer, the singer with her dog, riding horses and interacting with other animals. articles.title: 'Nana Patekar's final film 'Shakti Shalini' will be a tribute to the actor': Director Aditya Sarpotdar
articles.summary: Filmmaker Aditya Sarpotdar says he never imagined his upcoming horror-comedy 'Shakti Shalini' would be Nana Patekar's last film and will now ensure it
articles.body: Filmmaker Aditya Sarpotdar says he never imagined his upcoming horror-comedy 'Shakti Shalini' would be Nana Patekar's last film and will now ensure it serves as a fitting "tribute" to one of Indian cinema's finest actors."Shakti Shalini", the next title of Maddock Films' popular horror comedy universe, will posthumously feature Patekar alongside Aneet Padda of 'Saiyaara' fame.'Shakti Shalini' to be a tribute to Nana PatekarAccording to Sarpotdar, the actor, who passed away in the early hours of Thursday after suffering a heart attack in Goa, had completed shooting for the movie in May.He revealed that Patekar had spoken to him about 10 days ago, seeking an update on the film's post-production, and was looking forward to watching the movie."I never expected that 'Shakti Shalini' will be his last film. I'm deeply saddened that this will be his last work. I never thought that he would suddenly step away in this way. I'm unable to process what has actually happened. It (film) is going to be a tribute to one of the best actors of our cinema," Sarpotdar told PTI on phone from Berlin.Aditya Sarpotdar on narrating 'Shakti Shalini' script to Nana PatekarThe director, who is also a family friend of the celebrated actor, shared that he had approached Patekar twice for two of his earlier Marathi films, but things did not materialise."For him the script was the most important thing. If he liked the script, he would do the film; if not, then he wouldn't. I had written those two films keeping him in mind, and there's no replacement for him in Marathi cinema. He wasn't excited about it (film) and hence it didn't happen."The director recalled narrating the script of "Shakti Shalini" to Patekar at his farmhouse in Pune, after which the actor immediately agreed to join the project."He liked the story, his role, Aneet's role and the world that we were creating as well as the things we are talking about in the film. He was excited about 'Shakti Shalini'. We rather stayed for a few days at his farmhouse and had discussions and jammed over the script. He liked having a collaborative process," he said, without divulging details about Patekar's role in the movie."He wouldn't watch every film but he was aware about the horror-comedy universe, he had liked what we had made ('Stree', 'Munjya'). He only had good things to talk about it," the director added.Aditya Sarpotdar on working with Nana PatekarWorking with the 75-year-old actor turned out to be an enriching experience for Sarpotdar, who described Patekar as a "power house of a talent" and "childlike" person."He was always excited and inquisitive to know newer things, like he was interested to know about VFX, the thought process of the young actors and technicians, their working style, etc," he said.Aditya Sarpotdar admits Nana Patekar yelled at himSpeaking about Patekar's well-known outspoken nature and temper on the sets, Sarpotdar said he was occasionally reprimanded by the actor but never took it to heart."Yes, of course, he yelled at me. He would yell 'haq se'. He wanted everyone to put their best foot forward. He was a senior and experienced actor, and he had a point of view. He would want to express that, talk, discuss things, which he believed was good for the film and the filmmaker," he said.According to the filmmaker, Patekar's anger never lasted long."...Within five minutes he would come back, either pat me on the back, feed me something or hug me. That was the most endearing thing about him. You would automatically forget that he had yelled at you," he said.Nana Patekar's final films before death'Shakti Shalini', produced by Dinesh Vijan via his banner Maddock Films, is reportedly expected to arrive in theatres in March 2027.In addition to this film, Patekar will also be seen in the Shraddha Kapoor-starrer "Eetha", slated for release in December 2026, and director Anant Mahadevan's "The Confession of Mary".Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce branded ‘absentee’ owners over $5.35 million Ohio mansion; neighbours raise sewage, wildlife and security fears while couple’s team defends scaled-back fence and preserved access
articles.summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are facing objections from neighbours over plans to increase privacy and security at their $5.35 million mansion in
articles.body: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are facing objections from neighbours over plans to increase privacy and security at their $5.35 million mansion in Bratenahl, Ohio. The couple's proposed six-foot fence and extensive landscaping have sparked a dispute with longtime residents, who have raised concerns ranging from potential damage to a shared sewer line to wildlife safety and privacy.According to the Daily Mail, the disagreement has continued through local planning and architectural review meetings, with officials approving parts of the couple's proposals while asking them to revise other plans.Neighbour calls the new owner an 'absentee owner'Katherine Bolton, who has lived next door to the property for 35 years, reportedly described the arrival of the new owner as a major disruption to the peace and quiet of the Lake Erie village.At a meeting of Bratenahl's Architectural Review Board last month, Bolton criticised the prospect of an owner who would not be present at the property regularly.“There's a new owner, who is an absentee owner, who is not going to be here,” she said, according to the hearing transcript cited by the Daily Mail.The report said the couple's names were not mentioned during the 72-page transcript of that meeting. However, at a subsequent hearing on Tuesday, Bolton explicitly identified the property as having been purchased by Kelce.The mansion reportedly spans 21,000 square feet and includes eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms and a two-bedroom guest cottage. Built in 1895, the estate also features a ballroom that has been converted into a game room and home theatre.Shared sewer line becomes a major point of contentionOne of Bolton's principal concerns involves a century-old clay sewer pipe shared by her home and the mansion.She told the board that she had received an estimate of $75,000 to line the pipe to protect it against tree-root intrusion. Her concerns intensified after learning about the couple's proposed landscaping, which reportedly included planting around 50 evergreen trees near the sewer line.“Planting 50 evergreen trees just ten feet from a 100-year-old clay sewer line is virtually guaranteed to cause severe root intrusion, pipe structural failure and catastrophic sewage backups,” Bolton told the meeting, citing research she said she had conducted using artificial intelligence.She also questioned whether the new owners would remain in the area long enough to deal with any problems that might arise.The couple's project representatives disputed the criticism. Jacob Kutz of Tiny Construction told the board that Bolton had planted arborvitae trees directly over the sewer line, closer to it than the trees proposed by the new owners.Property manager Patrick Hyland also said the owners had spent $7,500 of their own money to replace a damaged section of the shared sewer line and had arranged for the entire line to be cleaned.According to the Daily Mail, the couple's team also said it had added gates to preserve Bolton's access to the sewer.Residents question fence design and security plansChuck Bauernschmidt, who has lived two doors away for 39 years, raised concerns about the removal of vegetation from the property. He presented photographs to the board and criticised what he described as the extensive clearing of shrubs and trees.“It's now ridiculous,” he said, according to the hearing transcript. “All the trees are gone.”Bauernschmidt also questioned the proposed fence's spear-topped design, warning that deer could become caught on its points. Village official Mary Ranney reportedly acknowledged that such incidents occur occasionally.Bolton's husband, Bill, a former president of the Bratenahl village council, raised further concerns about whether the fence would provide meaningful protection against paparazzi. He argued that a fence measuring five or six feet would not necessarily deter someone determined to look into the property.He also pointed to potential security threats from drones and Lake Erie, questioning how the owners might respond to unauthorised aerial surveillance.Board approves some plans but asks for revisionsThe couple's representatives reportedly said they had initially considered an eight-foot fence extending approximately 1,190 feet around the lakefront estate. Following discussions, the proposal was scaled back to a six-foot fence, which was unanimously approved at the earlier meeting despite objections from neighbours.The approved fence will replace an existing five-foot structure, sit two feet farther inside the property boundary and stop short of Lake Erie.At Tuesday's hearing, the board approved the proposed landscaping at the front of the estate, subject to conditions ensuring the trees on the southern side have sufficient room to mature.However, it declined to approve a proposed line of saplings along the shoreline, citing concerns about their eventual height. The couple's team must return with a revised landscaping plan.Photographs cited by the Daily Mail reportedly show landscaping work already underway, with sections of turf removed and bare ground visible. A “no trespassing” sign has also been placed at the entrance.Couple's team says it has tried to accommodate neighboursDespite the objections, representatives for Swift and Kelce told the board they had made several changes in an effort to maintain good relations with nearby residents.Kutz said the fence had been moved farther inside the property's boundary and that the plan to extend it to the water had been dropped. The team also said it had paid to cut back trees on the Boltons' and Stephensons' properties and had installed an additional gate after Bauernschmidt complained that he felt closed off.The property manager reportedly said neighbours would continue to be allowed to cross the back gardens with permission.Kutz also presented photographs to challenge claims that the estate's grounds had been stripped of healthy vegetation, arguing that the property had previously been heavily overgrown and poorly maintained.Not all residents opposed the changes. Victoria Broer, who chaired Bratenahl's planning commission for nearly 20 years, reportedly welcomed the decision to keep the fence away from the shoreline.“I do appreciate that the fence is not going all the way to the lake, because that would be in my view,” she said.Property records cited by the Daily Mail indicate that the mansion was purchased in March by a limited liability company linked to Kelce. The company had been incorporated in Ohio on February 26 and was used to acquire the property a week later.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Olivia Colman on viral Wicker memes: 'This has never happened to me before'
articles.summary: Steamy jokes have flooded social media ahead of the release of the actress's latest film.
articles.body:
It has already been described as 2026's weirdest rom-com .

And new film Wicker has sparked a deluge of viral memes and steamy jokes that have flooded social media ahead of its release.

Speaking to the BBC at its London Film Festival premiere, lead star Olivia Colman said she never expected such a big reaction.

"No, literally this has never happened for anything I've done before," she said.

"But you put Alexander Skarsgård in an interesting outfit, and everyone is looking."

The film tells the tale of a lonely, ostracised fisherwoman (Colman) living in a medieval village.

Tired of constantly being mocked for being single, she hires a basketmaker to mould her a new partner made entirely out of wicker.

Enter Skarsgård - but not as you've ever seen him before.

As the "wicker husband", he emerges as a strapping, dashing life-size piece of furniture.

And he proves to be a devoted partner, and passionate lover, sparking jealousy among the other village women.

The film has an A-list cast, with other stars including Peter Dinklage as the basket weaver, Elizabeth Debicki as the tailor's wife, and Richard E Grant as the village doctor.

Since the release of the trailer, there's been a huge buzz online around the film - from BookTok and FilmTok fans swooning over Skarsgård’s character, to questions being asked over splinter risks during the film's erotic scenes.

Swedish giant Ikea even got involved, posting photos of its rattan furniture on Instagram in a nod to the film, with the caption “husband material”.

When asked why she thinks people are so fascinated and so thirsty for the wicker husband, Colman answered: "We all love a little bit of escapism. That's what film is beautiful for.

"And it's magical, and a bit of fantasy, and people love that, especially currently. What's not to love about a little bit of escapism and fantasy?"

She also said it was the film's originality that drew her to it.

"You get a lot of scripts through the post, and you feel like you've seen a bit before. And this, I really hadn't seen this before, so I was excited," she said.

Like Colman, Debicki agrees that Skarsgård is the main reason the film has lit up the internet.

"I think it was a lot to do with Alex in a wicker man costume, really," she told the BBC. "I think that's something that apparently everybody would like to see."

But Skarsgård himself gives all the credit to the designers of the outfit. "All I had to do was get stuck into it," he says.

He also said the sex scenes were "super fun" to shoot.

"We wanted those moments when the bed crashes and breaks, and the way they comment on that in the scene is quite comedic," he said.

"But [the characters] also have tender moments and sexy moments, it was great."

The film is based on the short story The Wicker Husband by Ursula Wills-Jones.

After its premiere at Sundance film festival earlier this year, The Guardian awarded it two stars, praising the "eye-catching premise" but cautioning that there was "too much wood but not enough fire".

But The Hollywood Reporter was more positive, calling it "a warming, sometimes poignant pleasure".

Away from the social media buzz, the film's stars say it also taps into deeper themes, from gender roles to breaking societal rules.

"It's very funny and strange and wonderful, but I find it very moving. And it's a good one to discover beyond the Ikea memes," said Debicki.

"It touches on a lot of stuff. Hierarchy, social structure," said Skarsgård. "But it's done with such a light touch."

"It's about love, and it is funny, but it's also a romance, and it very gently laughs at the sort of traditions we have in marriage and community," said Colman.

"I think it's something that you will come out and discuss a lot."

Wicker is released in UK cinemas on October 30.

articles.title: Anti-Zuckerberg movie 'The Social Reckoning' takes critical heat on both sides of political aisle
articles.summary: Aaron Sorkin's "The Social Reckoning" faced blistering critiques from both conservatives and liberals and sits at 59% on Rotten Tomatoes.
articles.body: "The Social Reckoning," the follow-up to the 2010 hit "The Social Network," is facing blistering critiques from both sides of the political spectrum alongside lukewarm reviews from critics, with some reviewers sharply criticizing the film's political messaging and its handling of Facebook's role in American politics. "The Social Network" focused on the creation of Facebook and the legal battle over its ownership, earning three Oscars, including for screenwriter Aaron Sorkin, and a 96% positive rating on review-aggregation website Rotten Tomatoes. It's more political follow-up, "The Social Reckoning," written and directed by Sorkin, has received a more mixed response, with a 61% critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes as of Thursday evening. DAVID MARCUS: WOKE 1.0 IS WHY ENTERTAINERS NEEDED OUR SECRET CONSERVATIVE CLUB Earlier this year, a trailer debuted showing Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg (played by Jeremy Strong) being questioned by a character played by comedian Bill Burr. In the scene, Zuckerberg defends online free speech and argues that users are responsible for their own behavior. Burr’s character vigorously challenges him. Sorkin published an open letter in 2019 criticizing Zuckerberg’s management of the platform. OutKick writer Ian Miller was one of several conservative critics who mocked the trailer as tone-deaf, replying, "It is the most Hollywood thing ever to desperately try and convince everyone that the guy making complete sense is the bad guy and the one demanding authoritarian ideological enforcement is the good guy." Film critics were also sharply critical. The Globe and Mail film critic Barry Hertz tweeted that the film was "one of the most insipid, ugly, flat films of the year — an insufferably sanctimonious fantasia of blue-state Boomers." In his actual review, he argued that the movie is counterproductive in that it "will turn even the most hardcore Facebook hater into a true-blue Facebook believer — the film is just that magnificently, unbelievably, despicably bad." Variety said it badly missed the original's director David Fincher and "already feels behind the curve," while Wired magazine’s review described the new film as one that "already feels irrelevant." Wired noted that the movie opens with the DUI arrest of a woman who directs racist, right-wing insults at police officers and is arrested for threatening to kill one of them. When the video goes viral, a Facebook whistleblower recognizes the woman as a former liberal acquaintance from her Pilates class. The film's climax, as noted by Wired, is the Jan. 6, 2021, capitol riot, "the horrors of which are blamed in part on Facebook’s failure to either get a handle on election fraud conspiracy theories or remove Donald Trump’s account as he stoked such inflammatory falsehoods." "Now, halfway into Trump’s second term, is it all that much of a revelation that he and his movement are emboldened by the complicity of tech oligarchs, who openly backed him in 2024?" the outlet asked. CHRIS MURPHY CALLS FOR 'REGULATING THE INTERNET' SO PEOPLE WON'T FALL FOR A 'DEMAGOGUE LIKE DONALD TRUMP' Journalist and film critic Stephen Silver described the movie as "an old-man-yells-at-cloud treatment of Facebook." Silver wrote that Sorkin essentially argues Facebook was not censorious enough in the 2010s and that the government should now step in by reforming Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, a federal law that generally shields online platforms from liability for content posted by users. "No, I don’t buy that Facebook is primarily responsible for American political extremism, or for January 6," Silver wrote, arguing that individuals remain responsible for their own actions online. SFGate's Lindsey Bahr wrote that while certain political aspects hit the mark, the movie falls far short of its predecessor: "It is unfortunate for ‘The Social Reckoning’ that ‘The Social Network’ exists." IndieWire was even harsher, panning its script and performances. The BBC's reviewer gave it two out of five stars, calling it unlikely to influence anyone, while The Guardian in a mixed review dismissed it as a "film which doesn’t reckon with the future we’re living in." Even some reviews rated as positive on Rotten Tomatoes were tepid in their assessments. A review from The Seattle Times said it moved "snappily" but was still a "pale imitation" of "The Social Network." CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Media Research Center President David Bozell commented on the film's political messaging to Fox News Digital. "It says everything you need to know about Aaron Sorkin and the Hollywood elite that they would make a movie suggesting Big Tech’s real failure was not censoring conservatives enough," Bozell said. "The Media Research Center spent years exposing how Facebook suppressed conservative voices, and we were right to do it," he continued. "Mark Zuckerberg eventually acknowledged Meta’s past censorship abuses and took meaningful steps to move the company back toward a more open platform. Meta is far from perfect, but Zuckerberg deserves some credit for redirecting it away from the censorship monster it had become. "Hollywood seems determined to fight yesterday’s battle even as Zuckerberg has moved on from it," Bozell added. "Americans have had enough of government-imposed censorship, ideological gatekeeping and Big Tech deciding which political views they are allowed to hear." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Among the more positive reviews of the movie came from the San Francisco Chronicle, praising it as a "stirring journalistic thriller."

articles.title: Malhar Patekar on father Nana Patekar's legacy: 'His achievements have made him immortal' - WATCH
articles.summary: Veteran actor Nana Patekar's son Malhar Patekar said his father's work has made him immortal and that his vision, particularly his social initiatives
articles.body: Veteran actor Nana Patekar's son Malhar Patekar said his father's work has made him immortal and that his vision, particularly his social initiatives through the Naam Foundation, would be carried forward even after his demise.Speaking to reporters about his father's legacy, Malhar Patekar said, "A person like Nana Saheb never truly leaves us; his achievements have made him immortal. Secondly, he always believed that everyone should come together and follow a righteous path on a global scale. Thirdly, regarding the future-carrying forward the vision Nana Saheb left behind is how we will shape the life ahead."Elaborating on his father's vision and the work of the organisation, Malhar said, "Through our organisation, work was already underway in the water sector, and large-scale initiatives in education and health had begun in Kashmir as well. Thirdly, he assigned specific responsibilities to everyone before he left."Regarding the Marathwada work, he said, "I spoke to the Chief Minister just a short while ago, and he noted that the work being done through the Naam Foundation is proceeding under the guidance of our CEO, Ganesh Thorat. The Chief Minister acknowledged that we have collaborated in the past, but he emphasised that Nana Saheb had intended to push even harder this time around. So, the Chief Minister stated that we must ensure that what he had envisioned actually comes to pass."On the decision to conduct the last rites late Thursday night, Malhar said, "We proceeded (with the last rites today) because the tragedy occurred early this morning, so a significant amount of time had already passed. That is why we decided to go ahead with it today."Nana Patekar died after suffering a severe cardiac arrest. He was taken to Manipal Hospital, where doctors tried to revive him for around 45 minutes. Dr Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Oncology Department at Manipal Hospital, confirmed the news to ANI. He was laid to rest with full state honours in Pune, marking a solemn farewell to one of India's most celebrated actors.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'The Paradise' box office collection day 15 vs 'Don't Trouble The Trouble' day 7: Nani's film earns Rs 89 lakhs; worldwide gross reaches Rs 171.32 cr; Fahadh Faasil starrer collects Rs 4.41 cr India net
articles.summary: Nani's 'The Paradise' and Fahadh Faasil's 'Don't Trouble The Trouble' recorded further declines in their daily box-office collections on Thursday, October
articles.body: Nani's 'The Paradise' and Fahadh Faasil's 'Don't Trouble The Trouble' recorded further declines in their daily box-office collections on Thursday, October 8. According to Sacnilk, 'The Paradise' earned Rs 89 lakhs in India net collections on Day 15, while 'Don't Trouble The Trouble' collected Rs 25 lakhs on Day 7.'The Paradise' has accumulated Rs 118.98 cr in India net collections, with its domestic gross standing at Rs 140.17 cr. Its overseas gross has reached Rs 31.15 cr, taking the worldwide total to Rs 171.32 cr.Meanwhile, 'Don't Trouble The Trouble' has earned Rs 4.41 cr in India net collections. Its domestic gross currently stands at Rs 5.05 cr after seven days in theatres.The Paradise Day 15 box office collection'The Paradise' collected Rs 89 lakhs across 1,320 shows on Thursday. The figure marked a 7.3% drop from the previous day's Rs 96 lakhs. The Nani-starrer earned Rs 108.20 cr during its opening week. Its second-week collection reached Rs 10.78 cr, bringing the overall India net total to Rs 118.98 cr.The film recorded 96,070 footfalls on Day 15. Its Telugu 2D screenings registered an overall occupancy of 18.68%. Morning shows recorded 15.90% occupancy, while afternoon screenings reached 19.70%. Evening occupancy stood at 19.80%, followed by 17.70% for night shows.The Paradise day-wise collectionThe film earned Rs 2.80 cr on its second Friday, followed by Rs 2 cr on Saturday and Rs 2.10 cr on Sunday. Collections fell during the weekdays, with the latest figures showing a further decline.DayDateIndia net collectionShowsOccupancyDay 9 – FridayOctober 2Rs 2.80 cr1,54732.8%Day 10 – SaturdayOctober 3Rs 2 cr1,57324.3%Day 11 – SundayOctober 4Rs 2.10 cr1,58127.4%Day 12 – MondayOctober 5Rs 1.10 cr1,50319.3%Day 13 – TuesdayOctober 6Rs 93 lakhs 1,49918.4%Day 14 – WednesdayOctober 7Rs 96 lakhs 1,49119.0%Day 15 – ThursdayOctober 8Rs 89 lakhs1,32019.0%Don't Trouble The Trouble Day 7 box office collectionFahadh Faasil's 'Don't Trouble The Trouble' earned Rs 25 lakhs in India net collections on Thursday. The film recorded 611 shows, with its daily earnings falling 16.7% from Wednesday's Rs 30 lakhs.Its first-week India net collection reached Rs 4.41 cr, while the domestic gross stood at Rs 5.05 cr. The movie recorded 26,494 footfalls on Day 7, taking cumulative attendance to 383,935. The Telugu 2D release registered an overall occupancy of 8.76%. Morning shows recorded 6.08%, afternoon screenings reached 8.17%, and evening occupancy stood at 6.00%. Night shows recorded 8.25%.Don't Trouble The Trouble day-wise collectionThe film opened with Rs 1.65 cr on Friday, October 2. Its daily collections declined over the following days, reaching Rs 25 lakhs on Thursday.What are the films about?'The Paradise' features Nani in an action-driven story. Despite receiving mixed audience reviews after its theatrical release, the film has continued its box-office run into its third week.'Don't Trouble The Trouble' follows a magician who accidentally makes a young girl disappear.
